motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Establishing Fireworks Restrictions for 2022. Mayor Westmoreland noted the difficulty in defining firework restrictions to protect residents and the City due to the unique characteristics and abundance of natural open spaces areas. Unified Fire Authority (UFA) representatives have provided input in determining firework restrictions. High wind and weather also impact fire safety. Mr. Cook verified the City can only prohibit geographical boundaries and may not include weather restrictions in the prohibitions. Councilmember Curtis recommended employing an informational campaign to educate residents concerning aerial firework dangers and weather impacts. Councilmember Love requested to review the prohibited locations to verify the reasonability of the restriction to ensure identical standards were applied to all areas. Eagle Mountain City Council Meeting – April 19, 2022 Page 10 of 15 Councilmember Wright suggested approving the item with direction to staff to further evaluate Brandon Park, Sage Park, and Evans Ranch to determine if the subdivisions have a central area deemed safe for fireworks. Director of Administrative Services/City Recorder Fionnuala Kofoed explained firework restrictions are required to be provided to the County by May 1st. UFA Battalion Chief Embret Fossum stated that his understanding is that the restrictions must be set prior to May 1st, and cannot be amended afterward other than circumstances qualifying for the emergency clause. Mr. Cook explained Utah Code 15A-5-202 is an amendment to International Fire Code and cities must be in compliance with both documents when setting fire restrictions. Discussion ensued regarding the following: • The clarification that the proposed map is based upon staff and UFA recommendations and it is the purview of the Council to remove or add restricted areas; • Natural landscape and framed houses in neighborhoods undergoing construction increase fire hazards; • Enforcement and confusion with approved location considerations; • Restrictions assisting with establishing resident liability; • Historical data used as consideration for the restriction map may no longer be relevant if the characteristics of the region have changed; • Salt Lake City restricts fireworks in all areas east of 1300 East; • Scheduling to evaluate the map in-depth prior to the approval of restrictions for 2023; • Pursuing the City offering alternative forms of celebration; • The desire to establish uniform standards; • Law Enforcement discretion when issuing citations and liability restitution; and • Codifying permanently allowed and restricted areas and perimeter standards. Councilmember Love recommended including clarification that residents are liable for fire damage regardless of igniting fireworks in an allowed or prohibited area. Councilmember Wright believes the 2019 map has negative impacts on some residents. Nevertheless, the recommended restrictions represent a plan with previously vetted developments that has been implemented in the past and would allow the item to move forward within the requisite timeframe. He feels passionately that the proposed map should be reviewed in-depth and updated prior to approving firework restriction areas for 2023. He encouraged residents to be responsible and not ignite fireworks in restricted areas due to the high fire dangers. Ms. Kofoed suggested permitting fireworks at completed park parking lots within the restricted developments if deemed appropriate by staff. She explained that staff had been operating under the assumption that fireworks would be restricted City-wide this year until they received notification from UFA desiring an updated map. Eagle Mountain City Council Meeting – April 19, 2022 Page 11 of 15 Councilmember Curtis stated he had made potential amendments to the firework restrictions map to allow fireworks in some subdivisions. Councilmember Gray inquired if any of the areas include livestock. Councilmember Burnham expressed concern with areas potentially having large lots with highly combustible natural open space. Discussion ensued regarding opening City park parking lots to residents for fireworks uses, clarifying that church parking lots are private property and should not be used for fireworks, and providing information to the public to promote safety.
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to approve a resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, establishing fireworks restrictions for 2022 using the map in the staff report and authorizing City staff to designate City park locations in any restricted area as approved firework ignition sites. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
